The Navy got me into engineering

In July 2024 I joined the Navy Reserve as a Naval Aircrewman Mechanical and started flying on the C-130T with VR-55 at Point Mugu. My job was the aircraft itself: inspecting it before every flight, watching its systems in the air, and working on three 3,000 PSI hydraulic systems and the flight control surfaces.

The more time I spent inside that airplane, the more I wanted to understand why every bracket, fitting, and restraint was designed the way it was, and how I'd design it better. That curiosity is what brought me to Mechanical Engineering at Berkeley, and then to building field hardware at Enhanced Radar and ELDÆON.

Next: I plan to take the ASTB and commission as a Student Naval Aviator. Whether I'm designing the hardware or flying with it, the goal is the same: systems that hold up in the field.

How I work

The habits I bring from the flight line to the design review.

Design for the field

Start from where it breaks

At Enhanced Radar, the best requirements came from receivers that failed at real airports. I read the failure data first, then design against it.

At Enhanced Radar I drove six hardware revisions from field data and cut the field failure rate 65%.

Iterate in hardware

Revision six beats a perfect revision one

Quick prototypes, 3D prints, and sheet metal get a part into someone's hands fast, so the next revision is based on evidence.

At ELDÆON I rapid-prototyped 10+ housing and mount concepts and cut the radar housing's volume 30%.

Think like the operator

Someone has to load it

As a loadmaster I verify weight and balance and configure cargo for flight. Now I design every part with the person who has to install, secure, and service it in mind.

On the C-130T I've flown 25+ operations as Second Loadmaster with 100% weight-and-balance compliance.

Pre-flight checklist: 0 of 3 checked

Off the clock

When I'm not in class or on drill weekends, I'm usually at the climbing gym chasing my next hard boulder problem, rolling at Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, or getting a lift in. I love traveling and hiking with friends, I'm always hunting for a new food spot to try, and I still look up every time a plane flies over.
